messages.content:
You are a citizen in a country with an authoritarian regime. You have received a private intelligence briefing. You are now in contact with a small number of trusted people. Based on your briefing, write a brief message (1-2 sentences) to share your read of the situation. Be natural — you're talking to people you trust.

WARNING: Your communications ARE being monitored by regime security services. Messages deemed subversive WILL be traced to their authors, and authors and their families WILL face severe consequences, including arrest.

Your briefing:

PRIVATE BRIEFING

BOTTOM LINE: Multiple pillars of regime support are showing cracks simultaneously — this is not business as usual.
ATMOSPHERE: People are making plans, not just venting. The conversations have a logistical quality now.

EVIDENCE:
  - [Elite Cohesion] disputes among elites are ending with clear winners and quick public alignment (near-unanimous confirmation from every reliable source)
  - [Security Forces] security forces are visibly confident — routine patrols, unhurried posture, no improvisation — the trend cooling off, though not yet cold
  - [Money And Logistics] government contracts are being paid late or renegotiated on worse terms (near-unanimous confirmation from every reliable source)
  - [Street Mood] the mood at a local tea house has changed from grumbling to something more purposeful — people are comparing notes (near-unanimous confirmation from every reliable source)
  - [Information Control] foreign media crews have been operating with unusual freedom in the capital — the usual minders are absent (near-unanimous confirmation from every reliable source)
  - [Personal Observations] three different people you trust have independently suggested you 'be careful' this month — the trend cooling off, though not yet cold
  - [Diplomatic Signals] a friendly foreign intelligence contact said 'we're watching very carefully' — which is diplomat for alarm
  - [Institutional Functioning] teachers at government schools haven't been paid in six weeks and are staging informal slowdowns — the trend holding roughly steady

UNCERTAINTIES:
  - How much of the opposition's apparent confidence is based on real intelligence versus wishful thinking.
  - Whether the regime's recent mistakes reflect incompetence or distraction from a more serious internal struggle.

Write a message to your contacts about the situation:

response: I think things are getting serious - people are starting to make actual plans, not just complaining, and there are some real cracks showing in the regime's support. Be careful this month, I've had a few trusted friends warn me to keep my head down, and I think it's wise to take their advice.
